lead: Oceanside plumbing deals with salt air, hard water and slab homes from several eras. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Oceanside.
risk: slab leaks, salt-air corrosion and hard water scale
risk_short: slab leaks, corrosion and hard water
why: South Oceanside and Downtown have homes from the 1920s to the 1960s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Inland areas such as Rancho del Oro were built mostly after 1980 on slabs.
Salt air near the beach corrodes outdoor fittings and water heater parts. California requires water heaters to be strapped for earthquakes.
water: Oceanside blends imported water with local groundwater treated at its Mission Basin desalting plant. The water is hard.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Rinse and check outdoor fittings for corrosion.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in South Oceanside, Fire Mountain, Loma Alta, Mission San Luis Rey, Ocean Hills, Rancho del Oro and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Oceanside Building Division, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Does salt air affect plumbing in Oceanside?
faq.a: Yes. Salt air corrodes metal hose bibs, valves and water heater parts, especially within a mile or so of the beach. Check outdoor fittings each year and replace corroded parts early.
